memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died, yet his eyes were not weak nor his strength gone." — Deut 34:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a striking detail about Moses at the end of his life: at a hundred and twenty years old, "his eyes were not weak nor his strength gone." Moses did not fade away in feebleness; he remained clear-eyed and strong to the very end. His death was not the failing of a worn-out body, but the appointed conclusion of a life fully lived in God's service. God sustained His servant right up to the moment He called him home.

This tells us something about how God cares for those who walk with Him. Moses had poured out his whole life leading God's people, yet God kept him strong for the task until it was finished. There is a lovely truth here: God gives strength for the work He calls us to, sustaining us until our purpose is complete.

We often fear growing weak, losing our abilities, fading before our time. But our times are in God's hands. He is able to sustain us for as long as He has work for us to do. We can trust Him with our strength, our years, and the timing of our journey's end.

Whatever season you are in, remember that your life is held by God, who numbers your days and sustains you for His purposes. And for those in Christ, even when the body finally does grow weak, there is the promise of resurrection — new, imperishable strength in a body that will never fade (1 Cor 15:42-43). Moses' undimmed eyes point to the greater truth that in Christ, our best days are not behind us but ahead, in the life to come.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I trust God to sustain me for the work He has given me?
2. How does knowing my times are in God's hands ease my fears about the future?
3. How does the promise of resurrection change how I view growing older?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You sustain Your servants for the work You call them to. Help me trust You with my strength and my years, knowing my times are in Your hands. Thank You for the resurrection hope in Christ. Amen.
